case_name: Sathiyamoorthy and others v State Represented by Inspector of Police, Madurai
respondent:
State Represented by Inspector of Police, Madurai
Supreme Court of India

21 July 2014
Cr.A. No. 1169 of 2014(From the judgement and order Dt. 27/08/2012 in Cr.A No. 238/2006, of the MADRAS HIGH COURT)
(Non-Reportable)
The Judgment was delivered by : Ranjana Prakash Desai, J.
1. The appellants who are original Accused Nos. 1 to 6 respectively were tried in the court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Madurai in Sessions Case No.444 of 2005 for various offences under the Indian Penal Code (for short, "the IPC") on the allegation that on 11/11/2004 at about 8.00 p.m. when complainant Ayyanar and his son Murugesan were standing at a common place all the accused came there and formed an unlawful assembly with deadly weapons. Accused No. 2 unlawfully restrained Murugesan. Accused No. 1 attacked complainant-Ayyanar with an iron rod. He also attacked Murugesan with an aruval. Complainant Ayyanar lodged the FIR.

facts: The appellants who are original Accused Nos. 1 to 6 respectively were tried in the court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Madurai in Sessions Case No.444 of 2005 for various offences under the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'the IPC') on the allegation that on 11/11/2004 at about 8.00 p.m.
Accused No. 1 attacked complainant-Ayyanar with an iron rod.
He also attacked Murugesan with an aruval.
After completion of investigation, the accused were sent up for trial.
At the trial the prosecution examined 16 witnesses.
The accused denied the prosecution case.
issues: Whether the offences u/ss. 341 and 325 are compoundable
Whether the conviction of the appellants for the said offences can be reduced to the sentence already undergone by them
petitioner_arguments: The accused have paid a reasonable amount to victim Murugesan as per the decision of family elders and they have entered into an amicable settlement in their village much before the accused surrendered as per the orders of this Court.
In view of the settlement, this Court may compound the offences as that will accord a quietus to all disputes between the parties.
court_reasoning: However, offences u/ss. 148 and 149 of the IPC are not compoundable.

Since the accused and the victim have entered into a compromise, we feel that it would be in the interest of both sides to reduce the sentence awarded to the accused u/ss. 325 and 341 of the IPC to the sentence already undergone.
holding: The offences u/ss. 341 and 325 of the IPC, for which the appellants are convicted, are permitted to be compounded because they are compoundable.
The appellants are acquitted of the said offences.
The appellants are stated to have undergone more than six months imprisonment.

So far as offences u/ss. 148 and 149 of the IPC are concerned, the conviction of the appellants for the said offences is reduced to the sentence already undergone by them subject to the appellants paying Rs.30,000/- as compensation to victim-Murugesan.
